diff --git a/solution.sh b/solution.sh
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..156a457
--- /dev/null
+++ b/solution.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Integer-divide the first argument by the second.
+a="$1"
+b="$2"
+if [ "$b" -eq 0 ]; then
+  echo "Infinity"
+else
+  echo $(( a / b ))
+fi
prompt: The script solution.sh integer-divides its first argument by its second and prints the result. The division-by-zero handling is wrong: when the second argument is 0 it currently just prints "Infinity" to stdout and exits successfully, which hides the error from callers. Fix it so a zero divisor instead prints an error message to stderr, exits with a non-zero status, and prints nothing to stdout — while normal division still works (e.g. bash solution.sh 10 2 prints 5).
